residual_findings.title: Spec §3.2 show output missing Local time + Next fire (UTC) columns (spec completeness)
residual_findings.note: Spec example mandates 4 columns: Role / Cron / Local time / Next fire (UTC). Implementation renders only Role / Cron / Enabled. The whole point of per-Work cron config is 'let authors set the work on autopilot' — show is the primary verification surface. Fix: Local time = parse hour/minute fields of cron expression + render in TZ + cap at 3 entries with …; Next fire (UTC) = cron::Schedule::from_str(&normalize_cron_fields(expr)).upcoming(Utc).next() (single .next() per role, O(1)). render disabled when !enabled. Hermetic test asserts the two new columns.
residual_findings.closure_note: V1.50 T-A P0 fix-wave: 4-column `render_show` with Role / Cron / Local time / Next fire (UTC) columns. Single `.next()` per role (O(1)) for next-fire UTC; `local_time_display` parses min/hour fields; disabled state renders `--` / `disabled`. `render_show_includes_local_and_next_fire_columns` and `render_show_disabled_renders_disabled_for_next_fire` tests pass.

residual_findings.title: Spec §3.1 'all-off' rule not enforced (spec compliance)
residual_findings.scope: crates/nexus42/src/commands/creator/works/cron.rs :: CronCommand::Set (no --all-off flag) and apply_set_args (no all-disabled check)
residual_findings.note: Spec §3.1 verbatim: 'At least one role must remain enabled: true unless --all-off is passed (CLI rejects empty schedules).' Both --all-off flag and post-mutation check missing. `set my-work --no-brainstorm --no-write --no-review` succeeds silently. T-A P1 cron evaluator will then skip all fires indefinitely. Fix: add --all-off flag in CronCommand::Set clap; post-mutation count of enabled roles; if 0 and !all_off return CliError::Config with stable code (e.g. E_CRON_ALL_ROLES_DISABLED). Hermetic test apply_set_args_all_off_without_flag_rejects.
residual_findings.closure_note: V1.50 T-A P0 fix-wave: `--all-off` flag added to `CronCommand::Set` clap definition; `apply_set_args` post-mutation check rejects all-disabled with stable code `E_CRON_ALL_ROLES_DISABLED`. `apply_set_args_all_off_without_flag_rejects` and `..._with_flag_succeeds` tests pass. `cron set --help` documents --all-off. Cross-corroborated by qc1 (W2) and qc3 (W-001) re-review.

residual_findings.title: TZ silently clobbered on role-only patch operations (data consistency)
residual_findings.source: qc1 (architecture/maintainability) W1; corroborated by qc2/qc3 (no disagreement on the data-loss path)
residual_findings.note: Trigger: `set my-work --no-review` (or any patch omitting --tz) on a Work with custom TZ stored. handle_set folds env/default TZ into effective_args.tz unconditionally, then apply_set_args patches schedule.tz = resolved_tz, clobbering the previously-configured author TZ. Suggested fix: only fold env/default TZ when user explicitly resets (no-flags → defaults branch) or passes --tz; for patch operations without --tz leave base.tz unchanged. Recommend extracting TZ resolution into a pure helper (resolve_tz) for testability. Add regression test set_no_review_preserves_custom_tz.
residual_findings.closure_note: V1.50 T-A P0 fix-wave: `resolve_tz(args_tz, env) -> Option<String>` pure helper extracted; `handle_set` only folds env/default TZ on explicit reset or --tz; for role-only patch operations, base.tz is preserved. Regression test `set_no_review_preserves_custom_tz` passes; 3 unit tests cover the pure helper.

residual_findings.title: list_works_schedule unbounded — workspace-scale performance risk
residual_findings.note: SELECT work_ref, work_id, schedule_json FROM works WHERE creator_id = ? AND workspace_slug = ? ORDER BY updated_at DESC has no LIMIT. For N ~ 5000 Works (multi-author workspace) latency grows linearly and CLI output becomes unreadable. Existing list_works precedent uses WorkListFilters::limit/offset (default 100). Fix: add optional limit param on list_works_schedule (default 100), pass through handle_list via --limit <N> flag. Update unit test to assert the cap.
residual_findings.closure_note: V1.50 T-A P0 fix-wave: `limit: Option<u32>` parameter (default 100) added to `list_works_schedule` DAO; `LIMIT ?` SQL bound; `--limit <N>` clap flag in `CronCommand::List`. `list_works_schedule_applies_limit` (DAO) + `cron_list_help_documents_limit_flag` (CLI) tests pass.

residual_findings.title: handle_set read-modify-write TOCTOU window (reliability, P0 single-user small risk; P1 daemon-writer introduces real race)
residual_findings.target: V1.50 T-A P1 (daemon writer race window)
residual_findings.note: handle_set: get_schedule_json → apply_set_args → set_schedule_json. No transaction. T-A P1 will introduce a daemon-side cron writer (spec §4) — that writer will be the racing party. P0 single-user CLI risk is microsecond window. Fix at P1: extract set_schedule_json_tx (atomic SELECT-then-UPDATE-with-version) OR CAS via UPDATE ... WHERE schedule_json = ? retry on mismatch. P0 fix-wave adds in-code TODO marker at cron.rs:613. Plan-level residual carried to T-A P1.
residual_findings.closure_note: V1.50 T-A P1: `set_schedule_json_tx` transactional CAS implemented; `handle_set` (and the cron evaluator) use the atomic variant. 4 hermetic tests cover rejection on stale preimage, concurrent-writer serialisation, successful apply on matching preimage, and missing-work error. In-code TODO marker removed.
